title: As It Is Played: which wall is chance?
question: Machine selectors asked to choose eight online chess games 'as it is' built a small, even copy of the sixty they were given, more even than chance ever is. Can the people who see this work tell a chance draw from that copy, and how do they picture the games people play online?
purpose: Machine selectors chose eight games to show how people play chess online. Their eights look like the whole set in miniature, smoother than a random draw. A machine cannot tell whether people see that difference. Before you see the answer, we ask which wall you think is chance and two guesses about how online games end.
reading: We compare readers' choices with the right wall, and readers' guesses with the counts in 400 games drawn from 128,323 played on Lichess on 1 October 2026. We report how many chose right, the median guess and the number of answer sets. We make no claim about people in general, only about the readers of this work.

questions.prompt: Did you pick the chance wall correctly?
Of 100 rated games people play online, how many end in checkmate?
How many of the 100 are over before move 15?
